quests.hint: Listen for the deadline mentioned - end of today or the week.
quests.explanation: 'By the end of today' means before the day is over; 'by the end of the week' gives more time. Deadline phrases with 'by' are essential in workplace English. 'By' expresses a deadline; 'until' expresses duration.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you send me the report by the end of today?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you send me the report by the end of the week?

quests.hint: Notice whether she was promoted last month or last quarter.
quests.explanation: 'Last month' and 'last quarter' both refer to recent past periods. In business English, 'quarter' refers to a three-month period. Q1 is January–March, Q4 is October–December. Time precision matters in professional contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: She was promoted to a senior position last quarter.
quests.correctAnswer: She was promoted to a senior position last month.

quests.hint: Focus on whether they finished under budget or ahead of schedule.
quests.explanation: 'Under budget' means costing less than planned; 'ahead of schedule' means finishing earlier than planned. Both are positive project outcomes but measure different things. These are key phrases in professional English.
quests.textToSpeak: The team successfully completed the project under budget.
quests.correctAnswer: The team successfully completed the project ahead of schedule.

quests.hint: Listen for whether physical or mental activity reduces heart disease risk.
quests.explanation: 'Physical activity' uses the body; 'mental activity' engages the mind. Both have health benefits. In academic English, 'reduces the risk of' is a fixed collocation - you reduce risk, not lower or cut it.
quests.textToSpeak: Regular physical activity reduces the risk of heart disease.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular mental activity reduces the risk of heart disease.

quests.hint: Notice whether her back pain is called persistent or chronic.
quests.explanation: 'Persistent' means continuing for longer than expected; 'chronic' is a medical term meaning long-lasting, recurring, or constant. Both describe ongoing pain, but 'chronic' is more clinical and severe.
quests.textToSpeak: She saw a specialist about her persistent back pain.
quests.correctAnswer: She saw a specialist about her chronic back pain.

quests.hint: Pay attention to whether diet or lifestyle is described as essential.
quests.explanation: 'A balanced diet' and 'a balanced lifestyle' are both health concepts. Diet relates specifically to food; lifestyle encompasses diet, sleep, exercise, and stress management. Choosing the right word changes the scope of the claim.
quests.textToSpeak: A balanced diet is essential for maintaining good health.
quests.correctAnswer: A balanced lifestyle is essential for maintaining good health.

quests.hint: Listen for whether she studied business or public management.
quests.explanation: 'Business management' focuses on commercial organisations; 'public management' focuses on government and non-profit sectors. Both are postgraduate disciplines. 'She completed a postgraduate degree in...' is standard academic English.
quests.textToSpeak: She completed a postgraduate degree in business management.
quests.correctAnswer: She completed a postgraduate degree in public management.

quests.hint: Notice whether he gained experience in the charity or private sector.
quests.explanation: The 'charity sector' includes non-profit organisations; the 'private sector' includes profit-driven companies. These are two of the three main employment sectors in English (alongside the public sector). Very useful vocabulary.
quests.textToSpeak: He gained valuable experience working in the charity sector.
quests.correctAnswer: He gained valuable experience working in the private sector.

quests.hint: Focus on whether the scholarship covered the entire degree or the first year.
quests.explanation: 'The entire degree' means all years of study; 'the first year' means only year one. Scholarship coverage is an important practical distinction. 'The scholarship covered her fees for...' is a natural academic sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: The scholarship covered her fees for the entire degree.
quests.correctAnswer: The scholarship covered her fees for the first year.

quests.hint: Listen for whether the government introduced new regulations or new targets.
quests.explanation: 'Regulations' are legally binding rules; 'targets' are goals to aim for but not legally required. This is a crucial policy distinction. Governments 'introduce regulations' (mandatory) or 'set targets' (aspirational).
quests.textToSpeak: The government has introduced new regulations to reduce emissions.
quests.correctAnswer: The government has introduced new targets to reduce emissions.

quests.hint: Notice whether plastic or water pollution threatens marine life.
quests.explanation: 'Plastic pollution' comes from discarded plastic waste; 'water pollution' is a broader term covering chemical, biological, and physical contaminants. Both harm marine ecosystems but through different mechanisms.
quests.textToSpeak: Plastic pollution is a major threat to marine life.
quests.correctAnswer: Water pollution is a major threat to marine life.

quests.hint: Focus on whether people are choosing electric cars or public transport.
quests.explanation: 'Electric cars' are a private transport solution; 'public transport' is a shared solution. Both reduce environmental impact differently. 'More people are choosing X to help the environment' is a common trend statement.
quests.textToSpeak: More people are choosing electric cars to help the environment.
quests.correctAnswer: More people are choosing public transport to help the environment.

quests.hint: Listen for whether tourist numbers have declined or increased.
quests.explanation: 'Declined significantly' means fallen substantially; 'increased significantly' means risen substantially. These are complete opposites. In English, 'significantly' collocates with both decline and increase - always listen for the verb first.
quests.textToSpeak: The number of international tourists has declined significantly.
quests.correctAnswer: The number of international tourists has increased significantly.

quests.hint: Notice whether sustainable or eco-tourism is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Sustainable tourism' is the broader concept of responsible travel; 'eco-tourism' specifically involves nature-based travel with minimal environmental impact. Both aim to protect the environment, but eco-tourism is a subset.
quests.textToSpeak: Sustainable tourism aims to protect local cultures and nature.
quests.correctAnswer: Eco-tourism aims to protect local cultures and nature.

quests.hint: Focus on whether she prefers independent travel or group travel.
quests.explanation: 'Travelling independently' means making your own plans; 'travelling in groups' means with organised tours or companions. These are opposite travel styles. 'She prefers X over Y' is the standard comparison structure.
quests.textToSpeak: She prefers travelling independently over using a package tour.
quests.correctAnswer: She prefers travelling in groups over using a package tour.

quests.hint: Listen for whether the council plans to build or renovate housing.
quests.explanation: 'Build' means construct new; 'renovate' means improve existing. Both address housing needs but through different approaches. 'The city council has plans to...' is a common public sector sentence structure.
quests.textToSpeak: The city council has plans to build more affordable housing.
quests.correctAnswer: The city council has plans to renovate more affordable housing.

quests.hint: Notice whether income or education inequality is the problem.
quests.explanation: 'Income inequality' relates to differences in earnings; 'education inequality' relates to unequal access to learning. Both are forms of social inequality but with very different causes and solutions.
quests.textToSpeak: Inequality in income remains a significant problem in many countries.
quests.correctAnswer: Inequality in education remains a significant problem in many countries.

quests.hint: Focus on whether young people find it hard to buy or rent a home.
quests.explanation: 'Buy' involves a mortgage and permanent ownership; 'rent' involves monthly payments without ownership. In most cities, renting is easier but buying is more financially rewarding long-term. This is a very common discussion topic.
quests.textToSpeak: Many young people are finding it difficult to buy a home.
quests.correctAnswer: Many young people are finding it difficult to rent a home.

quests.hint: Listen for whether online or distance learning is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Online learning' uses the internet; 'distance learning' is the broader concept including correspondence and online methods. Both make education more accessible. These near-synonyms require careful listening in academic contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: Online learning has made education more accessible to everyone.
quests.correctAnswer: Distance learning has made education more accessible to everyone.

quests.hint: Notice whether screens or technology is replacing teaching.
quests.explanation: 'Screens' is more specific (referring to devices); 'technology' is broader. Both are used in debates about digital education. 'Some argue that...' is a hedging phrase that presents a view without fully endorsing it.
quests.textToSpeak: Some argue that screens are replacing traditional classroom teaching.
quests.correctAnswer: Some argue that technology is replacing traditional classroom teaching.

quests.hint: Pay attention to whether students have more information or resources.
quests.explanation: 'Information' means facts and data; 'resources' means learning tools and materials. Students today have access to both, but these are different things. 'Students today have access to far more...' compares past and present.
quests.textToSpeak: Students today have access to far more information than before.
quests.correctAnswer: Students today have access to far more resources than before.

quests.hint: Listen for whether English or Mandarin is most widely spoken as a second language.
quests.explanation: English is the most widely learned second language; Mandarin is the most spoken native language. This important distinction comes up often in language and global communication discussions.
quests.textToSpeak: English is the most widely spoken second language in the world.
quests.correctAnswer: Mandarin is the most widely spoken second language in the world.

quests.hint: Notice whether translation or communication software has improved.
quests.explanation: 'Translation software' converts text between languages; 'communication software' enables people to connect and communicate. Both have advanced with technology but serve different functions.
quests.textToSpeak: Translation software has improved significantly over recent years.
quests.correctAnswer: Communication software has improved significantly over recent years.

quests.hint: Focus on whether bilingualism advantages you in the job market or international business.
quests.explanation: 'The job market' is broad; 'international business' is a specific context. Both are real advantages of bilingualism. 'Gives you a significant advantage in...' is a common collocational phrase in career and language discussions.
quests.textToSpeak: Being bilingual gives you a significant advantage in the job market.
quests.correctAnswer: Being bilingual gives you a significant advantage in international business.

quests.hint: Listen for whether grandparents play a role in childcare or family traditions.
quests.explanation: 'Childcare arrangements' involves practical day-to-day care of children; 'family traditions' involves cultural practices passed between generations. Grandparents contribute to both, but these are very different roles.
quests.textToSpeak: Grandparents often play a crucial role in childcare arrangements.
quests.correctAnswer: Grandparents often play a crucial role in family traditions.

quests.hint: Notice whether working parents balance work-home or career-family.
quests.explanation: 'Work and home life' and 'career and family' are near-synonyms but with a nuance - 'career' has a more ambitious connotation than 'work'; 'family' is warmer than 'home life'. These subtle differences matter in English.
quests.textToSpeak: Working parents face constant pressure to balance work and home life.
quests.correctAnswer: Working parents face constant pressure to balance career and family.

quests.hint: Focus on whether many families live far from their extended or immediate family.
quests.explanation: 'Extended family' means grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins; 'immediate family' means parents, siblings, and children. These are key family vocabulary terms that express very different degrees of family relationship.
quests.textToSpeak: Many families today live far from their extended family members.
quests.correctAnswer: Many families today live far from their immediate family members.

quests.hint: Listen for whether a plant-based or vegetarian diet is mentioned.
quests.explanation: A 'plant-based diet' includes only plant foods (no meat, dairy, or eggs); 'vegetarian' excludes meat but may include dairy and eggs. These are related but distinct dietary categories - important to distinguish in health discussions.
quests.textToSpeak: A plant-based diet has been linked to lower rates of heart disease.
quests.correctAnswer: A vegetarian diet has been linked to lower rates of heart disease.

quests.hint: Notice whether processed foods are high in sugar or salt.
quests.explanation: 'High in sugar' and 'high in salt' are both concerns about processed food. Nutritionally, excess sugar is linked to diabetes; excess salt to high blood pressure. These are different health risks with different consequences.
quests.textToSpeak: Many processed foods contain high levels of sugar and fat.
quests.correctAnswer: Many processed foods contain high levels of salt and fat.

quests.hint: Pay attention to whether home cooking is healthier or cheaper than fast food.
quests.explanation: Both claims are true - home cooking is generally healthier AND cheaper than fast food. But the sentences make different claims. 'Generally + comparative adjective' is a good hedging strategy in English.
quests.textToSpeak: Cooking at home is generally healthier than eating fast food.
quests.correctAnswer: Cooking at home is generally cheaper than eating fast food.
